Main article: [Gymnastics at the 2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics "Gymnastics at the 2008 Summer Olympics")

**Women's artistic individual all-around** competition at the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") was held on August 15. at the [Beijing National Indoor Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing_National_Indoor_Stadium "Beijing National Indoor Stadium").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_artistic_individual_all-around#cite_note-SR-1)

For each competitor in the women's qualification, the scores[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_2008_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_artistic_individual_all-around#cite_note-2) for all four apparatus were summed to give an all-around qualification score. The top 24 competitors moved on to the individual all-around final, though nations were limited to two competitors each even if more qualified. In the individual all-around final, each gymnast competed on each apparatus again. Only scores from the final were used to determine final rankings.

The women's artistic individual all-around competition at the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") was held at the [North Greenwich Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Greenwich_Arena_1 "North Greenwich Arena 1") on 2 August.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_artistic_individual_all-around#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_artistic_individual_all-around#cite_note-SR-2)

## Format of competition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gymnastics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women%27s_artistic_individual_all-around&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Format of competition")]

The top 24 competitors in the [qualification round](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_artistic_qualification "Gymnastics at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's artistic qualification") (with a limit of two per country), based on combined scores on the four apparatuses, advanced to the individual all-around final. In the final, gymnasts performed on each apparatus again. Qualification scores were then ignored, with only final-round scores counting.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_artistic_individual_all-around#cite_note-3)

The **women's artistic team all-around** competition at the [1948 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Summer_Olympics "1948 Summer Olympics") was held at [Earls Court Exhibition Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earls_Court_Exhibition_Centre "Earls Court Exhibition Centre") on 13 and 14 August. It was the third appearance of the event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_1948_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_artistic_team_all-around#cite_note-SR-1)

## Competition format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gymnastics_at_the_1948_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women%27s_artistic_team_all-around&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Competition format")]

The gymnastics format continued to use the aggregation format used in 1928 and 1936, the previous appearances of the event. The parallel bars, however, were replaced by the [flying rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_rings "Flying rings") (the only time women competed using the flying rings in the Olympics).[](https://www.gymnastics-history.com/2021/12/1948-the-womens-rules-and-apparatus-norms-for-the-london-olympics/) Each nation entered a team of eight gymnasts. All entrants in the gymnastics competitions performed both a compulsory exercise and a voluntary exercise on the vault and beam, and a compulsory exercise on the flying rings, with the scores summed to give a final total. Each team also performed two group exercises. The top six individual scores on each team and the two group exercises were summed to give a team all-around score. No individual medals (for either all-around or apparatus) were awarded for women.

The **women's artistic individual all-around** competition at the [1952 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_Summer_Olympics "1952 Summer Olympics") was held at [Messuhalli, Exhibition Hall II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C3%B6%C3%B6l%C3%B6_Sports_Hall "Töölö Sports Hall") from 22 to 23 July. It was the first appearance of the event.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_1952_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_artistic_individual_all-around#cite_note-SR-1)

## Competition format

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Gymnastics_at_the_1952_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women%27s_artistic_individual_all-around&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Competition format")]

The gymnastics format continued to use the aggregation format. Each nation entered a team of eight gymnasts or up to three individual gymnasts. All entrants in the gymnastics competitions performed both a compulsory exercise and a voluntary exercise for each apparatus. The four apparatus that would become standard (floor, balance beam, uneven bars, and vault) were all used in the same Games for the first time.

No separate finals were contested.

For each individual exercise, five judges gave scores from 0 to 10 in one-tenth point increments. The top and bottom scores were discarded and the remaining three scores averaged to give the exercise total. Thus, exercise scores ranged from 0 to 10, apparatus scores from 0 to 20, and individual totals from 0 to 80.

For the vault, each competitor had two tries for each of the compulsory and voluntary vaults with the better score to count. For the other three apparatus exercises, the competitor had the option to make a second try only on the compulsory exercise—with the second attempt counting regardless of whether it was better than the first. For both compulsory and voluntary floor exercises, and voluntary exercises in the non-floor, non-vault apparatuses, only one attempt could be made.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnastics_at_the_1952_Summer_Olympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_artistic_individual_all-around#cite_note-OR442-2)
